terms.definitionEn: A method that calls a callback for each item and returns a new array of results.
A method that returns a new array containing items whose callback result is truthy.
A method that combines array items into one accumulated result.
A method that returns the first item satisfying a callback condition.
A method that checks whether at least one item satisfies a callback condition.
A method that checks whether each item satisfies a callback condition.
A function passed to an operation for it to invoke while processing values.
A function that tells a sorting operation the relative order of two values.
An ordering based on comparing text-like representations from left to right.
The running value passed from one reduction step to the next.
A callback that determines whether a value meets a condition.
An operation that returns a result without changing the original collection.

questions.question: What does map return?
options: A new array containing each callback result
The first item that passes a test
questions.explanation: map transforms each item and collects the callback results into a new array.
The callback adds one to each input element.
filter keeps the values whose even-number predicate is true.

questions.prompt: Fill the method that returns the first value greater than five.
questions.explanation: find returns the first element whose callback returns a truthy value.
find stops at and returns the first matching item, which is 8.

questions.question: Which items are kept by filter?
options: Items whose callback result is truthy
Every item transformed by the callback
Items whose callback result is a number
questions.explanation: filter uses each callback result to decide whether to retain that item.

questions.prompt: Write doubleValues(values), returning a new array with every number doubled.
questions.explanation: map applies the transformation once to each value.

questions.prompt: Fill the method that keeps only positive values.
questions.explanation: filter creates a collection of items meeting the predicate.

questions.prompt: Write product(values), returning the product of every number, or 1 for an empty array.
questions.explanation: Use 1 as the initial accumulator so the empty case has the multiplicative identity.
some is true because at least one value is odd.
The accumulator starts at zero and receives each added value.

questions.prompt: Fill the method that returns true only when each value is positive.
questions.explanation: every checks that the predicate holds for all array entries.

questions.prompt: Write keepLongWords(words, minimum), returning words whose length is at least minimum.
questions.explanation: filter keeps words meeting or exceeding the boundary.

questions.prompt: Fill the initial accumulator so summing an empty list returns zero.
questions.code:
const total = [].reduce((sum, n) => sum + n, ____);
console.log(total);
questions.explanation: An explicit initial value supports empty arrays and defines the accumulation start.

questions.question: What does some report for this array?
options: Whether at least one item satisfies the predicate
Whether every item satisfies the predicate
The first item that satisfies the predicate
A new array of matching items
questions.explanation: some answers a yes/no question about at least one matching value.

questions.prompt: Write firstAtLeast(values, limit), returning the first matching value or null if absent.
questions.explanation: find returns the first match; convert its no-match result to the requested null.

questions.question: Why can the default sort order be surprising for numbers?
options: Values are compared as strings by default
The array is copied before sorting
questions.explanation: Without a comparator, sort orders string representations lexicographically.
The numeric comparator orders the values from smallest to largest in place.

questions.prompt: Fill the comparator result for ascending numeric order.
questions.explanation: Returning a - b places smaller numbers before larger numbers.

questions.prompt: Write sortedCopy(values), returning numeric ascending order without changing values.
questions.explanation: Copy before calling the mutating sort method and provide a numeric comparator.
Without an initial value, reduce uses the first element as the starting accumulator.

questions.question: How do map and forEach differ in their typical result?
keyPoints: map returns a new array of callback results
questions.modelAnswer: map applies a callback and returns a new array containing its results. forEach is generally used to perform side effects for each value and does not return a transformed array.

questions.question: Why is an initial value often useful with reduce?
keyPoints: It defines the accumulator's starting value
It gives the empty-array case a result
It avoids consuming the first element as the initial accumulator
Choose an identity appropriate to the operation
questions.modelAnswer: An initial value defines what the accumulator starts with and what result an empty array should produce. For addition, zero is a natural identity; for multiplication, one is.

questions.question: What should you consider when sorting numbers with Array.prototype.sort?
keyPoints: Copy first when the original order must remain
questions.modelAnswer: The default sort compares string representations, so numbers may not appear in numeric order. Supply a comparator such as (a, b) => a - b, and copy the array first if you need to preserve the original.
